q: where did thumbs up come from
what does thumbs up mean historically
why do we give thumbs up
a: The thumbs up gesture has a long and complex history. A common myth claims it originated in ancient Roman gladiatorial games, where the emperor would signal whether a defeated gladiator should be spared (thumbs up) or killed (thumbs down). However, historical research suggests this is likely incorrect. The Roman gesture for death was actually the thumbs up (pollice verso, meaning turned thumb), while a closed fist or hidden thumb might have signaled mercy. The modern meaning of thumbs up as a positive gesture became popular in the 20th century, particularly through World War II pilots who used it to signal readiness. American GIs popularized the gesture in Europe during and after the war. The gesture spread globally through Hollywood films and television. In many cultures, the thumbs up is a positive sign meaning approval, OK, or good job. However, it's important to note that the gesture has negative meanings in some cultures: in parts of the Middle East, West Africa, and South America, it can be considered offensive. The modern use of thumbs up as an emoji (👍) has made it one of the most widely recognized digital gestures worldwide.
